habit_scope: Next-Gen CZ 3–5 2x6 @ 24 in OC for 1–2 story (w/ or w/o habitable attic). ALTERNATIVE_TO m-P08-stick-16oc-2x4. Not the 16 in 2x4 habit. 3-story bottom stays 16 in.
how_it_is_done: Same platform raise as stick (plates on deck, square, tilt) but 2x6 @ 24 in OC. Permitted 1- and 2-story (with or without habitable attic) per Next-Gen Tables 2–3. 3-story bottom story 2x6 or 3x4 @ 16 in OC — not this 24 in habit. Nonbearing 2x6 exterior @ 24 in, height <=20 ft (Table 3).

Double 2x6 top plate skips in-line framing at 24 in (Next-Gen p 4). 2x4 @ 24 in still needs joists/trusses/rafters >16 in OC landing within 5 in of stud (IRC 602.3.3 via Next-Gen) — that 2x4@24 path is not this method (AF&PA: 2x4 @ 24 one-story only if sheathing/siding spans).

Sheathing STILL 6 in edge / 12 in field (Next-Gen Table 12). 6d common N/P at 24 in for 3/8 in WSP; 3/8 in at 24 in only to 100B with 8d. 7/16 in @ 24 in: 8d common 6/12 is the ABTG WSP match. Fasteners 3/8 in from panel edges (APA). Do not glue wall panels. Cladding fasteners that must hit framing can force 16 in — stay 16 when the cladding schedule says so (Next-Gen).
Interior GWB min 1/2 in; at 24 in, screws-only 12 in OC (not 16) (Next-Gen p 24). D6: IRC WSP lengths still assume interior GWB — if omitted, lengthen bracing (ABTG).

Headers: Table 11 conventional (not rim) — most 4-ft openings one 2x6 jack + one king; larger typical-house openings a double jack. Nonbearing: no header; one king; >8 ft opening needs double 2x top plate or structural sheathing. Load-bearing alts named: insulated single (1-story/top, sawn <=6 ft / SCL <=7 ft); box header 3–5 ft with WSP 3 in OC (15/32 in Exposure 1, strong axis horizontal); insulated double (2-1/2 in rigid in 2x6 cavity).

Rim header sits on KINGS (not jacks) — openings <=4 ft often one 2x6 each side. Rim plies continuous, extend to kings; double rim >=6 in past king. Hangers if joist is over/next to opening or bearing <1-1/2 in sawn / <1-3/4 in I-joist. Table 5: 16 ft joist @ 16 in → 560 lb hanger; @ 24 in → 830 lb (40/12 psf). Do not mix sawn joists with EWP rim. 1st-floor rim + 2nd-floor single headers is a named combo. Hangers are CLASS (c-P08-connector-class), not the stick sit-on-jack habit.
2-stud corner: 16d box @ 12 in OC (Next-Gen Figs 2–4). Layout module 24 in with trusses (AF&PA; ch16 15-1/4 in first stud becomes the 24 in equivalent).
Raise sequence still Gap on YouTube (gap-yt-24oc-field-raise). Use ch16 tilt/brace holds; do not invent a 24 OC field-raise video.

when_this_beats_habit: 1–2 story when the program wants 2x6 cavities and fewer studs (Next-Gen CZ 3–5). Double 2x6 plate is what unlocks 24 in without in-line. Not the default.
when_this_is_a_bad_idea: 3-story bottom at 24 in (tables say 16). Cladding that must hit framing at 16. 2x4 @ 24 without in-line. Mixing this with Glencoe 8d@3. Treating 24 in as if sheathing nails change off 6/12.
why_tier1_never_learned_it: Habit is 16 in 2x4 (ch16 / AF&PA; AWC example even keeps 16 as practice). 24 in 2x6 is the energy/labor ALT, not what the carpenter learned first.
permit_gate: should be on drawings before permit
permit_gate_notes: 24 vs 16 is permit-gate (stud pack, headers, GWB screw spacing, cladding). Confirm with AHJ / engineer. Next-Gen is IRC-based CZ 3–5.
risk_if_swapped_late: 24 vs 16 after permit changes studs, plates, headers, drywall screws, and maybe cladding. Catch before permit.
plain_language_summary: This is the 2x6 at 24-inch alternate, not the usual 2x4 at 16. OK on 1- and 2-story; bottom of a 3-story stays 16. Double 2x6 plate so you do not have to line studs under joists. Sheathing nails are still 6 and 12 — 6d common is not permitted on 3/8 at 24. Most 4-foot holes get one jack and one king. A rim header sits on the kings and runs at least 6 inches past. If the siding has to hit a stud, you may be back to 16.
spanish_summary: Esta es la alternativa 2x6 a 24 pulgadas, no el 2x4 a 16 de siempre. Sirve en 1 y 2 pisos; el piso de abajo de 3 pisos se queda a 16. Doble placa 2x6 para no alinear postes con viguetas. Los clavos del forro siguen 6 y 12 — 6d common no va en 3/8 a 24. Un hueco de 4 pies lleva un jack y un king. El rim header apoya en los king y pasa 6 pulgadas. Si el revestimiento tiene que picar poste, vuelve a 16.
